methodology.execution: One system Chrome process and one loopback server, switched between frozen builds only after each fresh context closes.
methodology.cold: Fresh context per sample; service workers blocked; browser cache disabled; CDP emulates 100ms latency, 4Mbps down and 1Mbps up. CPU is not throttled.
methodology.ready: Wall time from navigation start to the game's ready signal. Each sample verifies 18 Resource Timing entries with nonzero transfer and manifest-matching byte lengths.
methodology.profile: No parse/draw instrumentation during formal samples.
methodology.bandwidthFloor: 3,697,784 GLB bytes at 4,000,000 bit/s require about 7.4 seconds of ideal serial transfer, before protocol and processing overhead.
limitations: Loopback CDP throttling is a controlled simulation, not a physical phone or real network.
Resource Timing byte counts and a ready signal do not prove byte-identical responses; separate passive-stream hash diagnostics cover that claim.
Five samples per side are descriptive, not a statistical guarantee; other host work can affect results.
The frozen baseline precedes the final UX CSS commit; any difference is not automatically attributable only to the loader.
Host CPU counters include the browser and all other processes; they do not isolate unrelated work.
